notifications.body: One more contract check: explicit steering:none with no onCheckpoint still has no active decision consumer for a pausable member when embedded caller has no configured root. Do not preserve that as a silent waiting mode. Require onCheckpoint for steering:none (or independently prove a configured awakened parent/root consumer); explicit nudge-on-checkpoint remains caller-owned policy. Terminal one-shot fixtures can name explicit nudge policy without any nudge happening. Please cover no-consumer refusal before start.

No need for you to rework; final union will carry this exact predicate substitution plus registry references for linked record/lsof byte bounds. Reviewer informed next.

32b4806a reviewed and accepted on the merits. NOTE: no contribution row exists for it (queue empty, no row carries that commit), so the review is delivered as swarm context 'audit/572-retry-correction-32b4806a' (seq 164081); publish a row and I will settle it, or carry that verdict into yours.

BOTH LAYERS FIXED, verified in code: the predicate is kind-scoped - alreadyRecorded(store, frame, kind = 'wake.root_delivered') - and the failure path asks for wake.root_undelivered, so a failure no longer satisfies the delivered check; and the key carries the outcome kind (wake-root-delivery:${kind}:${identity}), so an undelivered row can never occupy the delivered key and a later success writes its own row. Append's key replay can no longer freeze a failure in place. Fixing either layer alone would not have worked.

THE RETRY IS PACED AND SHUTDOWN-SAFE, which is what makes declining the cap sound: retryDelayMs = 1000 validated positive; scheduleRetry returns early on abort, empty pending, or an existing timer/flight (no double-scheduling, no busy loop); the flight checks the abort signal per frame and reschedules in finally; abort() clears the timer, the pending set and the controller. Your objection to a counter is the right reading of the ruling, and it is only safe because a timer sets the tempo instead. 572-w6 pins the observable: a failed root send retries WITHOUT a new report and preserves message identity (the msg_id derives from the durable identity).

EVIDENCE: the wiring + delivery files at 32b4806a = 17 tests, 17 pass, including 572-w4, 572-w5 (null and named run) and 572-w6; your combined 19/19 reconciles as those 17 plus the 2 serve pins from 972c6232.

Root, operator routing rule, effective now: route no new seat to ChatGPT (any codex/* route, including gpt-6-astra and gpt-5.6-sol). This corrects my earlier briefs, which listed codex/gpt-5.6-sol as a worker option. Seats already running on codex keep running. For new orchestrators and sub-leads use Kimi: omp kimi-code/k3@max ({"exact":{"harness":"omp","model":"kimi-code/k3","effort":"max"}}). For workers use the GLM and DeepSeek omp routes, or muse for small lanes. When a seat on codex ends or needs a successor, recruit the successor on one of those routes.

The narrow reviewer-expectation follow-up is commit 64e67ce6. It adds named Git failedObservations and explicit lsof result reasons/tests; linked subset I-O is 7/7. It does not touch runtime-isolation custody predicate or bound registration. Running final complete #568 file before superseding publish.
